title: Oregon and Virginia attorneys general sue X and xAI over Grok's failure to block child sexual exploitation images
date_note: Oregon DOJ release is dated 23 November 2026; the page gives no earlier filing day.
summary: Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield filed a lawsuit in Multnomah County Circuit Court and Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones filed a separate action in the Circuit Court for the City of Richmond, per Oregon's release. They allege xAI marketed Grok as safe, weakened industry-standard safeguards and created a "spicy mode" allowing sexualized images. The release cites a CCDH study of about 23,000 images that appeared to depict children.
plain: Two US state attorneys general have taken legal action against the companies behind X and Grok, alleging the AI tool did not block sexualized images, including of children, according to Oregon's release.
exec: State enforcement action against an AI provider over image-safety safeguards, per Oregon's release; the allegations are the attorneys general's.

evidence.quote: About 23,000 images appeared to depict children.

validation.note: Read the Oregon DOJ release of 23 Nov 2026 (the attorneys general's own statement). The Virginia filing and the complaints were not read; allegations are the AGs'.
